newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat heads lower again after paring losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat heads lower again after paring losses.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil headed lower late session Thursday after cutting earlier losses on talk of a catalytic cracker at Tosco's Bayway refinery in New Jersey going into maintenance turnaround.
"There was talk of the Tosco cat cracker going into turnround, and that helped both products," said a dealer.

At 1458, January heating oil was off 1.20 cents at 70.20 cents after hovering at around 70.80. January gasoline was off 0.41 cent a gallon at 69.15 cents. February crude followed refined products to stand 18 cents a barrel lower at $24.92.
Tosco declined comment on the market talk which involved the 140,000 barrel per day unit that had not regained full operating capacity after a fire shut it down two and a half weeks ago.
Volume was thin as many dealers extended their Christmas holiday through the end of the week. Traders still continued to push down heating oil prices amid talk of tepid demand.
Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, were seen rising by about 500,00 barrels in this evening's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk ((212-859-1761))
